title: world_genesis_frame/1 — ONE SSE frame of POST /worlds/genesis. A world build is a long authored act with intermediate results, so it streams for the same reason a beat does. Every frame names something that was really authored: `working` frames carry a line of the world's own language as each part lands, `world` is the terminal success carrying the id you can now enter, `refused` means the brief could not become a world and says why, `error` means the machine failed and says so without pretending to be the world's voice. There is deliberately no progress percentage, no ETA and no stage list — a client must never render a number nothing produced (frontend law 2).

stated.description: World-authored text on `working` and `refused`, an honest failure line on `error`. Renders VERBATIM — never rewritten, summarised or title-cased (frontend law 1).

id.description: The new world's id. Present on `world` only; this is what the client navigates to.

display_name.description: The world's name as authored. Present on `world` only.

tagline.description: The world's one line of fiction. Present on `world` only.

playable.description: Always true on a `world` frame: this frame is emitted after the transaction committed, and a committed genesis always stamped player_entity_id. A build that could not reach that point ends in `refused` or `error` with no world at all — there is no frame shape for a half-built world, because one is never created.
